candidate.title: MULTI-Seq
candidate.scope: The MULTI-Seq middle row of the supplied Illumina schematic: LMO sample labeling of three separate treatment-cell populations, pooling intact labeled cells, a broad scRNA-seq workflow, and the cell-linked expression/sample readout. The primary paper clarifies the DNA sample-tag and common cellular-barcode interface. MULTI-Seq is the poster capitalization of MULTI-seq. Neighboring SNRS and Hi-SCL rows are independent catalogue entries, not alternatives within this target. CMO and single-nucleus implementations discussed in the paper are not depicted target workflows here.

operations.label: scRNA-Seq workflow
operations.description: Process pooled labeled cells through the depicted broad single-cell RNA-sequencing block. Cell lysis makes endogenous mRNA and sample tags available for capture; cell-indexed DNA library products are generated from both. The paper resolves the common-cell-barcode interface and separate expression and sample-barcode library fractions inside this otherwise unexpanded block.
operations.mechanism: In the paper-supported implementation, the DNA tag’s 3′ poly-A domain mimics a transcript for capture on mRNA-capture beads in single-cell droplets. Endogenous mRNA is converted to cDNA. During the reverse-transcription stage, transcript-derived and synthetic-tag products acquire a common cell barcode. Gene-expression and barcode-derived products form separate sequencing-library fractions; the diagram does not show their internal preparation sequence.
operations.information_effect: Transfers gene-expression information from RNA to DNA products and sample identity from the synthetic DNA tag to barcode-library products; shared cellular indices connect these two measurements.
